current_activity: Goodwood: Second Army attacks with VIII Corps in the centre, I Corps on the left and II Canadian Corps on the right
notes: Event date: 18 July 1944 (Ellis, vol. I, pp. 336, 340). Event definition: General Dempsey's orders for 18 July: I Corps is to establish the 3rd Division on the east flank, VIII Corps is to establish its three armoured divisions in the Vimont, Garcelles-Secqueville and Hubert-Folie-Verrieres areas, and II Canadian Corps is to take Giberville and Vaucelles; troops of all three corps are engaged from the morning of 18 July (pp. 336 and 340). Event support: one source family (Ellis, the British official history). Ellis, Victory in the West, vol. I, p. 336: "Put shortly General Dempsey's orders to his corps commanders for July the 18th were as follows"; p. 340: "Though troops of all three corps were engaged simultaneously". Location: Orne bridgehead / east of Caen (existing place PL0265) with a precision of 10 km. Location approximate: the point is the bridgehead east of the Orne from which the attack started; it is not the Army headquarters. Location support: Ellis places the attack in the bridgehead east of the Orne (p. 335); the Army headquarters place is not stated. Commander: General Dempsey, the Second Army commander (Ellis, vol. I, pp. 336 and 386).

current_activity: Bluecoat: Second Army opens its attack south from Caumont with VIII and XXX Corps
notes: Event date: 30 July 1944 (Ellis, vol. I, p. 386). Event definition: Second Army opens the new attack from the Caumont sector on 30 July with VIII Corps (15th and 11th Armoured Divisions) and XXX Corps (43rd and 50th Divisions) and the 7th Armoured and Guards Armoured Divisions in reserve (pp. 386-388). Event support: one source family (Ellis, the British official history). Ellis, Victory in the West, vol. I, p. 386: "Second Army was therefore to regroup and to launch a new attack with not less than six divisions from the area of Caumont"; "the British opened a new attack". Location: Caumont-l'Eventé (existing place PL0071) with a precision of 5 km. Location approximate: the point is Caumont, from which the attack started; it is not the Army headquarters. Location support: Ellis names the area of Caumont as the start of the attack (p. 386); the Army headquarters place is not stated. Commander: General Dempsey, the Second Army commander (Ellis, vol. I, pp. 336 and 386).

current_activity: Second Army's drive to the Somme starts from the Vernon bridgehead with two armoured brigade groups of XXX Corps
notes: Event date: 29 August 1944, first light (Ellis, vol. I, p. 468). Event definition: At first light on 29 August two armoured brigade groups, spearheads of XXX Corps, start from the Vernon bridgehead in heavy rain and mist on the first stage of the Army's drive through north-eastern France into Belgium, with the task of forcing the Somme on both sides of Amiens and establishing two armoured divisions in the Amiens-St. Pol-Arras area; XII Corps is to start from Les Andelys the next morning (pp. 468-469). Event support: one source family (Ellis, the British official history). Ellis, Victory in the West, vol. I, p. 468: "At first light on the 29th two armoured brigade groups, screened by armoured cars, started out from the Vernon bridgehead in heavy rain and thick mist". Location: Vernon, Eure (new place) with a precision of 5 km. Location approximate: the point is Vernon, the bridgehead where the leading elements started; it is not the Army headquarters. Location support: Ellis names the Vernon bridgehead as the start line (p. 468); the Army headquarters is not named. Commander: General Dempsey, the Second Army commander (Ellis, vol. I, pp. 336 and 386).
